The petitioner being owner of property bearing no.1024/8, a well built up shop measuring 92.50 sq.m. in Khasra no.2981/989/449(1-1), 2676/974/447(1-12) and 988446(3-6) in commercial area of Subzi Mandi, Shahdara, Delhi (total covered area was measuring 214.40 Sq.

In view of the above reasons, this reference was filed by the petitioner before this Court.
3. The award under reference was challenged on various grounds inter alia that it is not sustainable on admitted facts.
LAC failed to appreciate entire revenue estate of Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara which was declared a commercial area.
The entire area had developed into a highly congested urban city.
The land prices in the locality are astronomical, whereas, compensation has been awarded at the rate of Rs.2805/- per sq. meter.
LAC ought to have held that prevailing land prices in the locality.
LAC failed to appreciate that there had been phenomenal rise in the land prices during last few years in Delhi and particularly in last two years.
LAC failed to appreciate that site under acquisition was fully developed and there was already provision of pucca roads, college, sabzi mandi etc.
All civic amenities were already available at the site, hence, land rates adopted by LAC were apparently much below prevailing rates/prices.
LAC failed to appreciate surroundings of site.

The site was surrounded by main GT Road passes by the north side LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs.
Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 4 of 16 and Shahdara Railway Station on the south side.
4. The land was valued as per residential rates provided by Land & Development Officer, Ministry of Urban Development, Government of India, New Delhi, which is contrary to law.

Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

During the course of argument, counsel for both the parties have apprised this Court that the market value with respect to the land acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. The Hon'ble High Court has assessed the said market value after allowing a reduction of 20% @
Rs.5865/- per sq. mtr. which was previously determined by my Ld. Predecessor.
20.

Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, location and topography and acquired vide the same award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon the judgment titled as 'Ali Mohammad Beigh & Ors. Vs. State of J&K' reported in AIR 2017 SC 1518 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court wherein it is held that "when the acquired lands are identical and similar LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 11 of 16 and the acquisition is for the same purpose, it would not be proper to discriminate between the land owners unless there are strong reasons".

sentences.text: Even otherwise, nothing substantial has been brought on record by either side to differ from the market value assessed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in one of the matters arising out of the same award and pertaining to the identical land.

Though respondent no.2- DMRC further argued that the SLP against the order of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the said case is still pending before the Hon'ble Supreme Court with respect to the determination of market value, however from the perusal of the record, it is observed that SLP filed by the respondents has already been dismissed, however, SLP filed by the petitioner, namely, Sh.
M.L. Gupta is still pending adjudication.
Thus, market value assessed by the Hon'ble High Court has reached finality qua the respondents.

Therefore, in the totality of circumstances, it is held that market value of the land in question acquired vide the same notification and same award is fixed @

sentences.text: His testimony has gone unassailed since he was not cross-examined on the aspect of limitation.
The proviso to Section 18 of L.A. Act provides for period of limitation during which an application for reference to the Court can be made to the Collector.

The same reads as under:-
"Section 18. Reference to Court:-
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made.
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award.

(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, which period shall first expire".

LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 16 Therefore, in view of the Section 18(2)(b) of L.A. Act, 1894 which provides that in case the claimant was neither present nor represented before the Collector at the time of passing of award nor received any notice U/s 12(2),
L.A. Act from the Collector, the limitation to file the petition for enhancement of the compensation would be six months from the date of Collector's award.

entities.text: LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 16
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the Collector's award came to be passed on 20.07.1999 and the instant reference petition U/s 18, L.A. Act was filed before the Ld. LAC on 02.11.1999 which is within the period of limitation.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial is brought on record on behalf of the respondent to show how the present reference is barred by limitation.
Thus, the respondents fails to discharge the onus to prove this issue.

Hence,
this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

opennyai_summary.PREAMBLE:
Shyam Sunder vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2023
In The Court of Sh. Ajay Garg,
 Additional District Judge-01, (East),
 Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
Lac No.63/2016
Cnr No. Dlet01-001225-2016
In the matter of :-
Sh. Shyam Sunder
S/o Sh. Ram Ashray
R/o Old Tejab Mill, Shahdara, Delhi
 .....Petitioner
 Versus
1.) Union of India
 Through Land Acquisition Collector
 Shahdara, Delhi
2.)
Delhi Metro Rail Corporation
 Barakhamba Road, New Delhi
.....Respondents
Award No. 01/1999-2000
Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara
Date of Institution : 31.01.2011
Reserved on : 15.12.2023
Date of Decision : 15.12.2023
Notification U/s 4 : F.7(35)/95-L&B/La/Ii/5430 dt.
 12.06.1997.
Notification U/s 6 : F.7(35)/95-L&B/Ii/9064 dt.
 28.07.1997
Notification U/s 17 : F.7(35)/95-L&B/Ii/9064 dt.
 28.07.1997
Lac No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 1 of 16
 Reference Petition U/s 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.
 Judgment
Shyam Sunder vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131472888/
1 1.
This judgment shall decide the reference petition no. 63/2016 preferred by petitioner, Sh. Shyam Sunder for the enhancement of the compensation against compulsory acquisition of his property bearing no.1024/8, in Khasra no.2981/989/449(1-1), 2676/974/447(1-12) and 988446(3-6) in commercial area of Subzi Mandi, Shahdara, Delhi, wherein G.T. Road was on one side and Bhola Nath Nagar was on the other side vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999, passed by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as 'LAC'), Shahdara, Delhi.
To decide the reference U/s 18 L.A. Act r/w statement U/s 19 of the Act sent by the LAC Delhi, the relevant dates and facts which are necessary for adjudication in the present matter are being given herein under:-
i) Date of notification U/s 4 of the Act : 12.06.1997 ii) Date of notification U/s 6 of the Act : 28.07.1997 iii) Date of award : 20.07.1999 iv) Area of the locality : Chandrawali @ Shahdara v) Project : MRTS, Delhi vi) The land use of area as per award : Residential vii) Petition referred to court on : 31.01.2011 2.
Background:-
The petitioner being owner of property bearing no.1024/8, a well built up shop measuring 92.50 sq.m. in Khasra no.2981/989/449(1-1), 2676/974/447(1-12) and 988446(3-6) in commercial area of Subzi Mandi, Shahdara, Delhi (total covered area was measuring 214.40 Sq.
mtrs.) LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 2 of 16 situated in the revenue estate of Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara, Delhi-110032, filed the present reference against the award No.1/1999-2000 passed on 20.07.1999, thereby assessing the market value of the land @
Rs.2805/- per sq. yard and for covered shop Rs.3,90,533/-, which is not acceptable to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.facts:
In order to assess the correct value of the said land, the LAC should have taken into consideration the sale deeds of the area.
This is a notional value for the purpose of levying taxes on LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 3 of 16 mortgage mutation and transfer of government properties by the government and not the correct value for the said land.
LAC failed to appreciate entire revenue estate of Village Chandrawali @ Shahdara which was declared a commercial area.
The entire area had developed into a highly congested urban city.
The land prices in the locality are astronomical, whereas, compensation has been awarded at the rate of Rs.2805/- per sq. meter.
LAC ought to have held that prevailing land prices in the locality.
LAC failed to appreciate that there had been phenomenal rise in the land prices during last few years in Delhi and particularly in last two years.
The alleged land rates were farcical, which cannot be said to be reasonable for determining market value of land in question.
LAC has not made any effort to determine the actual / prevailing market value of land.
The land was acquired for public purposes but was put to disposal of DMRC, so DMRC is effective and necessary party for adjudicating the reference and prayed that he be awarded compensation @ Rs.70,000/-
per sq. meter besides solatium and interest along-with all other benefits prescribed under the law.
Shyam Sunder vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131472888/
3 6.
The land in question was not surrounded by standing trees, boundary, well or male wall at the time of notification U/s 4 of L.A.
Act.
8.
The present reference petition is filed beyond the limitation period prescribed under law and is therefore time barred and hence, the present reference petition is liable to be LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 6 of 16 dismissed on this sole ground only.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the amount of compensation awarded to the petitioner is liable to be enhanced?
If so, at what rate? OPP.
2.
Whether the reference petition of the petitioner is time barred?
"Whether the amount of compensation awarded to the petitioner is liable to be enhanced?
If so, at what rate?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
During the course of argument, counsel for both the parties have apprised this Court that the market value with respect to the land acquired vide the same notification and same award has already been decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi vide judgment dated 07.06.2019 passed in the case titled as "Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta &
Ors.' in which the Hon'ble High Court has fixed the market value of the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtr. along-with statutory benefits.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since there is an authoritative pronouncement on the fair market value of the similar land placed in similar circumstances, location and topography and acquired vide the same award, this Court need not to delve further in this regard.
Even otherwise, two equals cannot be treated unequally.
In these circumstances, this Court is not inclined to go into any evidences or judgments relied upon by the parties to the instant petition in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble High Court in case titled as 'Union of India Vs. M.L. Gupta' wherein the market value for the properties acquired vide the same notification and same award have already been assessed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mtrs. as on the date of notification i.e. 12.06.1997.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial has been brought on record by either side to differ from the market value assessed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in one of the matters arising out of the same award and pertaining to the identical land.
LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 13 of 16 Therefore, in view of the Section 18(2)(b) of L.A. Act, 1894 which provides that in case the claimant was neither present nor represented before the Collector at the time of passing of award nor received any notice U/s 12(2),
L.A. Act from the Collector, the limitation to file the petition for enhancement of the compensation would be six months from the date of Collector's award.
In the instant case, the Collector's award came to be passed on 20.07.1999 and the instant reference petition U/s 18, L.A. Act was filed before the Ld. LAC on 02.11.1999 which is within the period of limitation.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial is brought on record on behalf of the respondent to show how the present reference is barred by limitation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence,
this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
In view of the findings on issue no.1, the petition/ reference filed U/s 18 of L.A.
Act, is allowed.
The petitioner had claimed compensation of Rs.70,000/- per sq.mt.,
which is now fixed and allowed @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mt.
The petitioner is entitled to the market value @ Rs.4692/- per sq.mt. as on 12.06.1997 with respect to his share determined in the land acquired i.e. 115 sq.mtrs. as per the judgment in reference U/s Shyam Sunder vs Union Of India on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131472888/
According to the award, 12% interest was allowed on the market value, fixed by the LAC U/s 23(1)A of LA Act, 1894 from the date of notification U/s 4 of Act (12.06.1997) till the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999.
Accordingly, the same is also allowed on the present market value, fixed as above.
24. According to the award, interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894 was also allowed observing that DMRC had taken the land and as such petitioner is entitled to interest on the balance amount, as per section 34 of LA Act, 1894 @ 9% per annum from the date of possession i.e. 20.07.1999 till expiry of one year and thereafter, @ 15% per annum till payment or deposited into the Court.
The same is also allowed on the enhanced market value of the land in question, as determined above, subject to deduction of the interest for the period w.e.f. 30.01.2018 till 16.09.2023 as per order dated 16.09.2023 in Misc. DJ No.27/23 titled as "Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India" placed on judicial record.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation as determined hereinabove to the petitioner.
25. During the course of arguments, it is submitted that the respondent no.2- DMRC has already deposited the enhanced amount of compensation @ Rs.5865/- per sq.mt. and therefore the balance amount, if any, after payment of the decreetal amount to the petitioner, be sent back to respondent no.2.
However, if LAC No.63/16 Sh. Shyam Sunder Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 15 of 16 any additional amount requires to be deposited by respondent no.2 in terms of the present judgment,
the same be remitted by respondent no.2 with immediate effect.
26. The above reliefs are subject to the deductions of compensation / solatium / additional benefits / interest U/s 34 of LA Act, 1894, which have already been received by the petitioner as were fixed by the LAC vide Award No. 01/1999-2000 dated 20.07.1999.
The reference petition stands answered accordingly.
Both the parties will bear their own costs.
27. A copy of this judgment be sent to LAC concerned to make the payment of the enhanced amount of compensation to the petitioner within three months from today.
No order as to cost.
